newsitem.title: USA: Theragenics buys equipment, sets financing.
newsitem.headline: Theragenics buys equipment, sets financing.

text.p: Theragenics Corp said it agreed to purchase four additional cyclotrons used to make its Theraseed product, a radioactive implantable device the size of a grain of rice used to treat localized prostate cancer.
The first of these cyclotrons is expected to be on line in March 1998 and the final cyclotron is secheduled to be on line by the end of 1998, the company said in a statement.
Theragenics declined to identify the supplier of the cyclotrons. The company already has four cyclotrons in operation.
Each cyclotron costs about $4 million and Theragenics said the purchase represents a major capital expenditure in its efforts to supply anticipated increases in demand.

In a related activity, Theragenics also said it increased to $11 million from $5 million a credit agreement with Nationsbank which will provide funding for the purchase and for the company's planned relocation of its production and headquarters facilities to Buford, Ga.
The cost of the new cyclotrons and the relocation is estimated at about $20 million.
Shares of Theragenics were trading up 39/64 to 26-3/8.
